Every AI you use learned by walking downhill in the dark.
Training starts with a model that is basically random, and it gets everything wrong.
The wrongness is measured as one number, called the loss.
Picture that loss as a landscape. High ground means bad answers, low ground means good ones.
The model can't see the whole map. It only feels the slope under its feet.
So it takes one small step in the downhill direction. That slope is called the gradient.
Then it measures again, and steps again.
Repeat that billions of times, and the loss sinks.
The step size matters. Too big and it overshoots the valley. Too small and it never arrives.
